desc:
Among all contiguous subarrays of nums whose length is between lo and hi (both inclusive), return the largest possible sum. At least one such subarray exists.

nums = [2, -1, 3, -4, 5], lo = 2, hi = 3
length 2 sums: 1, 2, -1, 1      length 3 sums: 4, -2, 4
result = 4
hints: Trying every start with every allowed length costs O(n * (hi - lo + 1)). Use prefix sums so that any subarray sum is a difference of two numbers.
With prefix sums P, the subarray ending at j with length len has sum P[j] - P[j - len]. For a fixed j, you want the smallest P[i] with j - hi ≤ i ≤ j - lo.
That is a window minimum over a range of prefix indices that slides right by one for every j. Maintain it with an increasing deque of indices.
editorial: Let P[0] = 0 and P[i] = nums[0] + ... + nums[i-1]. A subarray occupying positions i..j-1 has sum P[j] - P[i] and length j - i. For each end j from lo to n the allowed starts are i in [j - hi, j - lo], so the best sum ending there is P[j] minus the minimum of P over that index range.

Both ends of the index range move right by one when j increases by one. Keep a deque of indices with increasing P values: push index j - lo (popping larger values from the back), drop front indices below j - hi, and read the minimum at the front. O(n) time and O(n) space. For hi = n this degenerates to the classic "best subarray of length at least lo".
